text:
maria: Heads-up — during the new sample app walkthrough a couple of customers hit a weird failure mode. SDK (py) returned a generic RuntimeError for auth expiry and 429s, confusing users.

sam: Ugh. Do we have a canonical error shape? I thought we landed on typed exceptions earlier but maybe not consistent across SDKs.

jordan: Not consistent. JS throws a structured `RedwoodError` with `code` and `details`; py currently raises `RuntimeError` in one place and a thin `HTTPError` in another.

lee: Quick question: are folks OK with adding small fields to the error surface (e.g., `retry_after`, `user_action`, `status_class`)? We want things to be machine-friendly for clients.

alex: +1 for machine-friendly. Proposed minimal shape we discussed: ```json
{
  "error_type": "rate_limit",
  "code": "rate_limit.exceeded",
  "status": 429,
  "retry_after": 12,
  "message": "Too many requests",
  "docs_url": "https://docs.redwood.ai/errors#rate_limit"
}
```

maria: That looks good. For auth, something like: ```json
{
  "error_type": "auth",
  "code": "auth.token_expired",
  "status": 401,
  "user_action": "refresh_token",
  "message": "API key expired",
  "docs_url": "https://docs.redwood.ai/errors#auth"
}
```

sam: We should avoid breaking changes for existing SDK users. Proposal: 1) keep current exceptions as-is but add new typed subclass (e.g., `RedwoodAuthError`, `RedwoodRateLimitError`) that wraps legacy. 2) expose raw `status` and `retry_after` in attributes.

jordan: Agrees. Also need parity matrix: which SDKs already include `retry_after`? Which return 429 as 4xx vs. map to transient?

lee: I'll draft a parity checklist. Minimal items: mapping table for 4xx/5xx -> typed exception, SDK exception class names, attribute names (`code`, `retry_after`, `docs_url`), sample app error handling snippet.

alex: Sample app snippet suggestion (py): ```py
try:
    client.generate(...)
except RedwoodRateLimitError as e:
    sleep(e.retry_after or 1)
    retry()
except RedwoodAuthError as e:
    show_login_prompt()
except Exception as e:
    logger.error("unexpected", exc_info=e)
    raise
```

maria: Can we make the sample app show user-friendly copy? People saw a raw stacktrace. Maybe fallback text like: "Service temporarily busy — try again in a few seconds" with an opt-in debug toggle.

sam: Good UX call. Also add a CI lint for sample apps to run codepaths that exercise rate-limit and auth flows so we don't regress.

jordan: Also worth deciding: map 429 -> `TooManyRequests` typed error (no retry by default) vs. `RateLimit` variant that exposes `burst_allowed`? We have customers who rely on `retry_after` header.

lee: For now, surface `retry_after` when header present; keep `status` accessible. Longer term we can add richer rate-limit metadata.

devx-bot: CI: sample-apps/test-error-handling passed on branch error-shape-proposal (build #482). :white_check_mark:

alex: Next steps I propose: 1) RFC doc with concrete JSON schema for error payload (backwards-compatible), 2) SDK change sets for py/js/go adding typed subclasses, 3) update sample app to catch typed errors and show friendly copy + debug toggle, 4) add CI test to exercise these paths.

maria: Thanks — can someone own the RFC? I can draft the user-facing examples and sample-app changes.

sam: I'll take SDK parity tracker and a PR checklist.

jordan: I'll add a small test harness for the JS SDK and run it against sample app flow.

lee: I'll open a short RFC PR today. ETA EOD. If anyone has nitpicks about field names (`code` vs `error_code`, `status` vs `http_status`), drop them here.

alex: FWIW I prefer `code` and `status` for brevity. Keep `error_type` optional.

maria: +1. One last ask: include a clear migration note in the SDK changelog and callouts in the onboarding docs so customers know to switch from catch-all RuntimeError patterns.

sam: Noted. I'll add changelog template.

jordan: Nice. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

maria: I'll follow up with a short list of sample app copy suggestions and a couple of screenshots once the PR lands.

lee: Great — marking owner: lee (RFC), sam (parity tracker), maria (sample app copy).
